clinician.trajectory_summary: A 38-year-old transgender female on 15 months of estradiol and spironolactone presented to the ED in June 2016 with progressive right-sided scrotal swelling, abdominal and back pain, fatigue, and 7 kg weight loss. Laboratory evaluation revealed markedly elevated tumor markers: LDH 5294 U/L, β-hCG 2526 IU/L, and AFP <2.5 μg/L, consistent with a non-seminomatous germ cell tumor. CT imaging of the abdomen/pelvis identified a right groin lesion (6.4 × 4.9 × 6.3 cm) and a large retroperitoneal mass (11.5 × 10.6 × 17.4 cm) causing right-sided hydronephrosis. CT thorax revealed left-side neck adenopathy (3 × 3 cm) without parenchymal lung lesions, confirming distant metastatic disease. Medical Oncology initiated BEP (bleomycin, etoposide, cisplatin) chemotherapy and advised discontinuation of hormonal therapy. A radical right inguinal orchiectomy was performed in October 2016, which showed scarring related to treatment effect with no residual malignancy, consistent with chemotherapy response. The combination of elevated tumor markers, metastatic disease to retroperitoneal lymph nodes and distant sites (neck adenopathy), and the clinical presentation established a diagnosis of stage IIIC germ cell tumor.
